idiom_name: PrefixParselet/InfixParselet interfaces + EnumMap of parselets (Bantam shape)
implementation_notes: Nystrom's Bantam is the reference Java realization: PrefixParselet and InfixParselet functional interfaces, an EnumMap from token type to parselet, and a parseExpression(minPrecedence) loop, with the infix parselet owning its precedence and a lookahead helper deciding whether the next operator binds tightly enough. Nothing in the JDK parses expressions for you, so the structure is hand-written; Java 8 lambdas collapse the one-class-per-parselet bookkeeping into a few registration lines, and an EnumMap keyed by an enum TokenType keeps the hot lookup allocation-free. Keep the table while error positions, AST shape and recovery matter; hand the grammar to ANTLR or JavaCC when it grows past its expression layer, or when generated diagnostics are worth more than hand-written ones.
pitfalls: A missing EnumMap entry returns null and the NullPointerException surfaces far from the offending token; register an error parselet or validate table completeness when the parser is built.

The parselet decides the recursion power, so associativity is a data-dependent detail: a right-associative operator must parse its right operand with its own precedence and a left-associative one with precedence + 1, and swapping them misparses only chained expressions.

Java has no tail calls and a fixed thread stack: deeply nested input raises StackOverflowError, which is catchable but usually leaves the parse state unusable, so impose a depth limit before the JVM does.
